claims.text: Undoped MnNiSi-based alloy has a large magnetocaloric effect.
Undoped MnNiSi-based alloy has inherently low mechanical toughness or brittleness.
Substituting approximately 3 wt% of Mn with Fe and applying the specified heat treatment will form coherent nanoscale Fe-rich precipitates.
The Fe-rich precipitates will be located primarily at grain boundaries.
Annealing at approximately 850°C for 12 hours under argon facilitates formation of the proposed nanoscale precipitates.
Rapid cooling will lock in the nanoscale precipitate distribution.
The proposed annealing regime can form precipitates without altering the primary crystal structure needed for the magnetocaloric effect.
Fine Fe-rich precipitates impede microcrack propagation.
Impeding microcrack propagation reinforces grain boundaries and improves overall mechanical toughness.
A minimal Fe substitution level avoids substantially perturbing the magnetic interactions responsible for the magnetostructural transition.
The magnetostructural phase transition produces the large magnetocaloric effect in MnNiSi-based material.
The intervention could approximately double fracture toughness relative to undoped MnNiSi.
The intervention will limit the decrease in magnetocaloric entropy change to less than 10% relative to undoped MnNiSi.
The predicted benefits will persist under cyclic thermal and magnetic stresses representative of magnetic-refrigeration operation.
Deviating from the proposed Fe concentration or annealing protocol may reduce the mechanical improvement or adversely affect magnetocaloric properties.
Excessive Fe can disrupt the magnetic interactions associated with the magnetocaloric transition.
Imprecise heat treatment or cyclic operation can cause precipitate coarsening.
Precipitate coarsening during cyclic operation can undermine the mechanical improvement.
